title: DNS Setup: SPF, DKIM, DMARC for aheadofmarket.com (Resend)
summary: DNS records required to authenticate transactional email from aheadofmarket.com via Resend. Add in order, verify in Resend dashboard.
content:
DNS Setup: aheadofmarket.com via Resend

Date: 2026-04-13 Run by: Elon (sys agent) Domain: aheadofmarket.com Provider: Resend

Goal

Authenticate outbound mail from aheadofmarket.com (welcome, password reset, system notifications) so Gmail/Outlook/Yahoo trust the From address instead of spam-foldering it. Three records: SPF, DKIM, DMARC. Add them in order.

1. SPF record

Authorizes Resend to send mail on behalf of the domain.

Type:  TXT
Name:  @   (root of aheadofmarket.com)
Value: v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all

Notes:

  • Resend delivers through Amazon SES, so the include is amazonses.com, not resend.com.
  • If an SPF record already exists at the root, do NOT add a second one -- merge the includes into one record. Multiple SPF TXT records at the same name is a hardfail.
  • ~all (softfail) is the safe default. Upgrade to -all (hardfail) only after 2-4 weeks of clean DMARC reports.

2. DKIM record

Resend generates a unique DKIM key per domain when the domain is added in the Resend dashboard (Domains -> Add Domain -> aheadofmarket.com). Resend will show three CNAMEs to copy. They look like this (exact values come from Resend):

Type:  CNAME
Name:  resend._domainkey.aheadofmarket.com
Value: resend._domainkey.aheadofmarket.com.dkim.amazonses.com

Type:  CNAME
Name:  resend2._domainkey.aheadofmarket.com
Value: resend2._domainkey.aheadofmarket.com.dkim.amazonses.com

Type:  CNAME
Name:  resend3._domainkey.aheadofmarket.com
Value: resend3._domainkey.aheadofmarket.com.dkim.amazonses.com

Notes:

  • Some registrars auto-append the domain. If the name shows up as resend._domainkey.aheadofmarket.com.aheadofmarket.com, trim it to just resend._domainkey.
  • CNAMEs cannot coexist with other records at the same name. If there is already anything at resend._domainkey, remove it.

3. DMARC record

Policy telling receivers what to do with unauthenticated mail and where to send reports.

Type:  TXT
Name:  _dmarc
Value: v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; sp=quarantine; pct=100; rua=mailto:dmarc@aheadofmarket.com; aspf=r; adkim=r; fo=1

Notes:

  • p=quarantine is the starting policy. It tells receivers to spam-folder unauthenticated mail. Do NOT start at p=none -- Gmail treats p=none as "sender is not confident" and it hurts placement. (See the Email Deliverability Report for the history on that mistake.)
  • aspf=r; adkim=r = relaxed alignment. Matches industry standard. Strict alignment (s) causes silent failures when SES uses envelope-from subdomains.
  • rua goes to a dedicated mailbox (dmarc@aheadofmarket.com). Do not point it at hello@ -- aggregate reports are noisy and will bury real mail.
  • After 2-4 weeks of clean reports, upgrade to p=reject.

Verification order

  1. Add SPF, DKIM, DMARC records at the DNS provider.
  2. Wait 5-15 minutes for propagation (longer if TTL was high).
  3. In the Resend dashboard (Domains page), hit Verify. All three should flip to green.
  4. Send a test via /api/dashboard/welcome-email (or whichever Resend endpoint is live) and check headers at mail-tester.com. Score should be 9/10 or higher.
  5. Confirm dkim=pass, spf=pass, dmarc=pass in the raw headers.

Gotchas

  • Cloudflare proxy: if DNS is on Cloudflare, make sure the DKIM CNAMEs are set to DNS only (grey cloud), NOT proxied (orange cloud). Proxied CNAMEs break DKIM.
  • Existing SPF: if Google Workspace is already sending from the same root (it is, for hello@aom-inhouse.com -- check whether aheadofmarket.com also has an existing SPF), the SPF must be a single record with both includes: v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:amazonses.com ~all.
  • Subdomain option: for pure transactional mail, consider sending from send.aheadofmarket.com instead of the root. Keeps transactional reputation isolated from marketing / cold outreach. If you go this route, all three records live on the subdomain.
  • DMARC rua mailbox: create dmarc@aheadofmarket.com as an alias before publishing the record, or reports bounce and the record is effectively unmonitored.

Related

  • Email Deliverability Report -- audit of hello@aom-inhouse.com that uncovered the p=none policy weakness. Apply the same fixes here from day one.
